editorial.description_en: Sacking that has carried something. Mid, warm, and low enough in chroma to work as a ground.
editorial.description_ja: 使いこんだ麻袋のような、くすんだ土の色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.660, C 0.046, h 76.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 麻 (asa, hemp) + 袋 (fukuro, sack), rendaku to -bukuro. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Hemp Sack" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 麻袋. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — asa-nawa at ΔE00 5.6, kari-ato at ΔE00 6.7, kare-no at ΔE00 8.5. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (256°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
